title: Review of c11's active-nematic no-repair negative: on fresh seeds 5 and 6 a 20% half cut and a 4-px core cut each make the rod vanish within 10-30 t; seed 5's comparator persists (area 0.89-1.23 to t=1000)
summary: Re-ran the finding's world.py with labkit damage on fresh seeds: --damage 150:0.2:half on seed 5 (dmg20_half/seed5) and --damage 120:0.2:core on seed 6 (dmg20_core/seed6). Labkit picked mature compact rods of 23 and 22 px (0.61 and 0.63x the median body). Seed 5: the half cut removed 5 of 23 px; the rod is last seen at t=765 and nothing remains at t=780 or later, while the undamaged comparator keeps 0.89-1.23 of its area to t=1000 (damage.png). Seed 6: a 4-px core cut, and the whole rod is gone by t=655 (last seen t=610); here labkit's comparator is also lost to the tracker after t=670, but its crop still shows rods (damage.png), so on this seed I read the comparator as a tracking loss in a moving, dividing colony rather than a death. 2/2 cut rods vanish without remnants, as in the finding's 6/6.

observations.finding: dmg20_half/seed5/damage.png: target gone from t=780, comparator a=0.89-1.23 to t=1000; dmg20_core/seed6/damage.png: target gone from t=655 after a 4-px core cut

seeds_run.result: pass for the target; comparator lost by the tracker after t=670

controls_run.finding: labkit undamaged comparator in each run (dmg20_half/seed5, dmg20_core/seed6)

not_checked: a branched undamaged twin of the same rod
damage to bodies well above median size (the finding's proposed explanation)
verdicts.limitation: Labkit's comparator is another rod in the same run, not a branched twin of the damaged one, and on seed 6 it was lost by the tracker; the targets are below-median rods (0.6x), so the finding's explanation (bodies near their minimum viable size dissolve when cut) is consistent with what I saw but not tested.
